evidence: PARTIAL runtime confirmation, with a required measurement gap, not a demonstrated missing-package defect. Frozen task/tests/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template. Lines 1-4 supply Node 22 and Python 3.12; lines 16-22 install claude-code 2.1.281, Playwright MCP 0.0.79, express 5.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.4.1; line 31 pins harbor-rewardkit 0.1.7; lines 33-38 install Chromium through that pinned Playwright package and expose /usr/local/bin/chromium. The app manifest dependencies at solution/app/package.json:13-15 match the runtime packages in both Dockerfiles. The verifier copies /tests at lines 43-45. Actual indexed build-verifier.log:58-63 records image sha256:a6e377e2468671fe2b676f3d211ca5c0cfdc4b68a98cffd1349b332ed59c6251. Its SHA256 is 2422e9feed050ab7a2b160cbf1067cc35007ed5003007cc6ede08e5e362ddbec, verified against the current index. artifact-binding.json (SHA256 22e8e05333a99e1b01b771789bf0c64dcb10e2cb539bd815270d02811ddcd6db, verified) binds all 15 packaged verifier files to the frozen tests. Installed configured-inspection/results.json (SHA256 06c999a26c56bf9c378f0ffcea682d35422f1002d4cfc0c545817183e4340bcf, verified) parses all five dimensions, resolves context and criteria, builds response schemas and constructs the configured claude-code/model arguments. The 133-criterion functional prompt is 99,776 bytes and the OS argument launch returns 0. Its 15 tests_sha256 values independently match frozen files. However inspect-configured.py explicitly substitutes /usr/bin/true for the executable during argument testing; only claude --version is actually run, so this is neither a Claude grading invocation nor provider evidence. Indexed mcp/results.json (SHA256 bad8d80ee96bda6a46775d4dfcc508371b96c50e3106cd9f4e27ffee1a6e4cc3, verified) records Playwright MCP 0.0.79 tools/list and working Linux Chromium browser operations, separate-context sign-in/readback, request overlap, and response-loss handling. Both 13-file source maps match the frozen app. This probe uses a local MCP package path and port 3032; it is supporting tool feasibility, not execution of test.sh and its configured judge. Indexed install-lifecycle/results.json (SHA256 368261834b06931f2e8ac0fa0fd909a435e7ae28a6c30444c3ff48240d27bb24, verified) and its inspected driver establish installation, sanitized unprivileged launch from /tests, actual restart MCP process replacement and durable data; all 13 app source hashes match the frozen snapshot. No full configured provider grading run is supplied, the index explicitly disclaims it, and runtime-evidence.json is absent. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md and qc/README.md require a hash-bound full verifier launch/grading record before clearance; successful build/parser/browser/lifecycle probes cannot supply that measurement. No Oracle, hosted QC or model score is inferred.
counterexample: Adversarial assessment, not a claimed measured grading failure: a health-responsive static shell with dead business controls can run in this fully equipped image and satisfy build/version/parser/OS-argument checks, which therefore cannot establish that the configured judge grades correctly. Conversely, a conforming app using the documented Node runtime and dependencies can launch successfully yet receive test.sh's initialized ungraded zero if the actual provider/CLI path fails before suite completion (test.sh:8,60,207-214). The current probes never exercise that path, so they cannot rule out this false-failure mechanism.
suggested_fix: When provider execution is authorized and credentials are available, run the frozen candidate through the actual configured verifier and retain hash-bound app, judge/MCP, suite, scorer and reward logs plus a runtime-evidence.json record; preserve the shared template and keep this evidence gap open until that run exists.
